claims.text: Evenly dispersed carbide nanoparticles in a high-entropy-alloy intermediate layer will enhance heat-transfer capability.
Carbide-nanoparticle reinforcement will preserve the structural integrity of the intermediate layer under plasma-facing reactor conditions.
Plasma-facing intermediate layers typically experience temperatures of approximately 800–1000°C together with cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
The intervention will produce a uniform distribution of carbide nanoparticles within the alloy microstructure.
Carbide nanoparticles form preferential thermal pathways through the alloy.
The preferential thermal pathways improve heat conduction.
Improved heat conduction reduces local temperature gradients.
A controlled nanoparticle dispersion limits disruption of the load-bearing alloy microstructure.
Limiting disruption of the load-bearing microstructure maintains mechanical strength.
Nanoparticle-reinforced layers will have moderately higher thermal conductivity than otherwise equivalent unreinforced layers.
Nanoparticle-reinforced layers will exhibit no significant degradation in cyclic mechanical endurance relative to unreinforced layers.
The predicted improvement depends on attaining a uniform nanoparticle distribution at an optimal volume fraction.
Nanoparticle agglomeration could compromise the mechanical integrity of the alloy.
Excessive nanoparticle loading could compromise the mechanical integrity of the alloy.
